page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the KVM hypervisor. It runs on a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor using the x86_64 architecture, providing 16 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory is configured at 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware acceleration flags include AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside cryptographic extensions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes a 10 Gbps baseline network interface. It features no integrated local storage or hardware GPUs, necessitating network-attached block storage for persistence.

Benchmark results place the instance consistently within the middle 50% tier across synthetic and application-level workloads. It achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,505.0 and a single-core score of 1,541.0, paired with a PassMark CPU score of 21,023.63. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth registers at 94.57 GB/sec, while write operations reach 55.52 GB/sec. Application testing reveals a Redis throughput of 15.62 million SET operations per second and static web serving throughput of 21.05 GB/sec. In language model execution, it processes 1,294.06 prompt tokens per second on lightweight 135M models, though performance drops to 31.85 tokens per second on 7B parameter models.

The 1:4 compute-to-RAM balance delivers predictable resource density for enterprise application tiers without the cost overhead associated with specialized hardware accelerators or memory-heavy classes. Because there is no bundled local storage, storage performance depends entirely on external network block volumes. The ecs.g7.4xlarge is well suited for web application serving, backend microservices, caching layers, continuous integration pipelines, and medium-scale relational or in-memory databases.

It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 64.0 GB of system memory, and a 10 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage for persistence. In standardized benchmarks, it demonstrates steady mid-tier capability, recording a PassMark CPU score of 21,023.63, a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,505.0, and a memory read bandwidth of 94.57 GB/sec on large blocks. It also yields 15.62 million SET operations per second in Redis tests. By maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance provides cost-effective resource allocation for general enterprise workloads, backend microservices, Redis caching nodes, and containerized application deployments.
